articleTitle: Decade bandwidth MMIC analogue phase shifter
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Multi-Octave Microwave Circuits
abstract: The design and simulated performance for a monolithic two-stage cascaded-match reflection-type phase shifter (CMRTPS), which employs decade bandwidth active circulators, is presented. It will be shown that a very low phase error characteristic can be obtained over a decade bandwidth with this novel topology. In addition, the phase shifter exhibits an excellent input return loss performance across this decade bandwidth.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Multi-Octave Microwave Circuits
abstract: Four different MMIC distributed mixers are described and compared. The first is a mixer using a cascode of FETs, the second is a matrix distributed mixer, the third is a balanced mixer using common-source and common-gate FET pairs, and the fourth is a double-balanced mixer using an active RF/LO combiner and an active balun.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Microwave and millimetre wave monopulse comparators
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Multi-Octave Microwave Circuits
abstract: Integrated 180 degrees coupler circuits are described for use in monopulse direction finding systems. Sigma - Delta Magic-T performance is obtained by using an almost 0 dB coupler and a -3 dB coupler.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: The design and realisation of broadband stripline circulators for the 18-40 GHz frequency range
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Multi-Octave Microwave Circuits
abstract: A computer-aided design procedure has been produced which enables circulator parameters to be calculated. The main input parameters are frequency range, ferrite saturation magnetisation and dielectric constant and the dielectric constant of the material surrounding the ferrite. An optimisation routine calculates the ferrite radius and coupling angle in order to maximise performance over the given band. S-parameter data files are generated which are compatible for inclusion as user defined elements within circuit files of both Super Compact and Touchstone. This enables the overall circulator design, including suitable matching elements connected to the junction ports, to be completed.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Multi-Octave Microwave Circuits
abstract: Time domain sampling techniques at microwave frequency have been used in frequency counters and sampling scopes. A microwave sampler is useful, in general, for very wide band system applications, both for time domain and frequency domain down conversion. This paper describes a 0.5-20 GHz hybrid microwave sampler which has a number of novel features to improve performance.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Wideband measurements on Vivaldi travelling wave antennas
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Multi-Octave Microwave Circuits
abstract: Wideband antennas are finding increasing application in the detection of electromagnetic interference, signals surveillance, the transmission and reception of short duration pulses, frequency hopping radar systems and multichannel discrete frequency communications. The principal broadband radiating elements used to date are 'broadside' radiating spiral antennas, 'endfire' log-periodic arrays and tapered slotline geometries. This contribution is concerned with the latter group of antennas which includes linearly tapered (LTSA), exponentially tapered (Vivaldi) or constant width (CWSA) slotline sections.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Design of a scalar analyser test head for time domain measurement
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Multi-Octave Microwave Circuits
abstract: Establishes the principles of performing time domain measurements using commercially available scalar analysers. In the analysis a number of assumptions concerning the microwave hardware were incorporated. These assumptions must be approximated to in a practical system due to limitations of the calibration/correction route. This article describes the design and implementation of a microwave test head which makes possible accurate time domain measurement using a scalar network system.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>
